title: Evaluate a postfix expression
prompt:
tokens is a valid postfix (reverse Polish) expression. Operands are integer strings such as "12" or "-3"; operators are "+", "-" and "*". Return the value.

- 1 to 10,000 tokens. Every intermediate result stays between -10^12 and 10^12.
- In postfix, "a b -" means a - b.
hints: Operands appear before the operator that uses them. Which data structure gives you the most recent operands first?
Push numbers. When you see an operator, pop two values.
The first pop is the right operand b, the second is the left operand a; push a op b. The final stack holds the answer.

solution.explanation: A stack holds operands waiting for an operator. Each operator consumes the two most recent operands. Pop order matters for subtraction: the top of the stack is the right-hand operand. Checking "-" by exact equality keeps "-3" a number.

complexity.notes: Each token is pushed or popped a constant number of times.
